meta.spec_reference: Standard MIDI Files 1.0 (MMA RP-001, the SMF specification) for the MThd/MTrk chunk framing, the variable-length quantity encoding, the delta-time model and the meta-event catalogue; the MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification (MMA) for the channel voice status bytes, the running-status rule, the seven-bit data-byte invariant and System Exclusive message structure; MMA RP-019 for the SMPTE timebase encoding. Decoder behaviour was measured against two independent implementations: TiMidity++ readmidi.c and mido 1.x midifiles.

schema_extensions.name: measured_gate
schema_extensions.why: An object of {decoders, observed, conclusion} recording what real parsers did when a field was set wrongly. MIDI has no checksums and almost nothing self-describing beyond the chunk lengths, so nearly every tier here had to be settled by experiment. Two parsers were used because they disagree in ways that change the answer: mido enforces the seven-bit data-byte rule, the key-signature range, chunk lengths and the running-status precondition, while TiMidity++ enforces none of those but is the only one that rejects SMF format values above 2. A field was assigned Tier A when either parser refuses the file, since a generator cannot know which the harness will use.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.why: The status byte's legal set is not a contiguous range: 0xF1-0xF6 and 0xF8-0xFE are System Common and System Real-Time messages that exist on the MIDI wire but are not permitted inside a Standard MIDI File. The template nevertheless routes all of them to sysex_event, which reads a length prefix they do not have. Listing them as excluded rather than silently omitting them records both the measurement that they break mido and the template gap that makes them reachable. The key is used only on a Tier A field, never to narrow a Tier C one.

schema_extensions.name: template_parse_requirement
schema_extensions.why: Separates rules that come from this template's construction from rules that come from the MIDI format. Three matter and all three change what a generator may emit: MidiHeader is a fixed six-byte struct so m_seclen can only be 6; the tempo field is a 24-bit bitfield inside a uint followed by a compensating FSeek(FTell()-1) at line 208, so it nets three bytes only if that seek is reproduced; and MidiTrack's loop subtracts from an unsigned counter and tests for exactly zero, so an inexact m_seclen underflows and runs away.

schema_extensions.name: tier on a diversity axis
schema_extensions.why: Eight of the twelve axes are Tier A fields. That is not a contradiction: the parser pins the legal SET - status bytes to 243 values, data bytes to bit 7 clear, formats to three, delta times to four bytes - but which member of that set a file uses is a completely free choice that reshapes the event stream. 'must_remain_unconstrained' on such an axis means emit the whole legal set, not the convenient member. The tier_note says which reading applies.

schema_extensions.name: cross_check
schema_extensions.why: Recorded for consistency with the sibling extractions, where a second evidence line was needed for fields declared in one place and constrained in another. This template has no such case: every constraint is established at the declaration site or comes from the specification, and the one field name with two declarations, meta_event.m_name at lines 167 and 171, is covered by a note rather than a second line.

meta.structure_note: A MIDI file is a flat sequence of chunks - one MThd header followed by m_ntracks MTrk tracks - each chunk a four-byte identifier and a big-endian length, with no nesting, no checksums and no terminator. Inside a track the bytes are a self-clocking event stream: a variable-length delta time, then a status byte whose high nibble decides how many bytes follow, and a status byte may be omitted entirely to reuse the previous one. That statefulness, not any compressed blob, is where this format's depth lies - one wrong byte desynchronises everything after it. The format does have one payload with required internal structure, the System Exclusive message, whose bytes must all be seven-bit with an 0xF7 terminator; every other byte run in the template is genuinely free-form text or unknown-meta data.
meta.no_checksum_note: MIDI has no checksum, CRC or Adler field anywhere. Checklist items 1 and 2 were re-scanned specifically: the only Tier A fixed_values are the two chunk identifiers MThd and MTrk, and the only calculated_values are MidiHeader.m_seclen, MidiTrack.m_seclen, meta_event.m_length and sysex_event.m_length. The absence is a property of the format, not an omission here.
meta.running_status_note: The single most important thing about this format for a generator. A message may omit its status byte and inherit the previous one, which the template implements at lines 67-70 by testing bit 7 and seeking back one byte. Three rules follow, all recorded as dependencies and structure rules: the first message of a track must carry an explicit status byte; a message after a meta or System Exclusive event must carry one too, because system messages cancel running status; and the generator must track the last status itself, because the number of bytes a running-status message occupies is decided by a byte that is not in the message.
meta.decoder_disagreement_note: The two parsers measured do not agree on what a valid MIDI file is. mido is the stricter on content: it alone enforces the seven-bit data-byte rule, the -7..7 key signature range, the 0/1 mode flag, exact chunk lengths, and the requirement that running status have something to continue from. TiMidity++ is stricter on one structural point only - it refuses SMF formats above 2, which mido accepts without comment - and otherwise resynchronises past almost any damage. Where they differ, the stricter answer was taken.
meta.measurement_note: Every gate marked measured_gate was established empirically. A parameterised SMF builder was written, a 41-byte format 0 baseline was verified to parse in both tools, and roughly 130 single-field mutations were run across both chunk identifiers, both chunk lengths, the format, track count and timebase, every status byte family on three channels, all eighteen meta types plus four undefined ones, meta payload lengths, the key-signature and time-signature payload values, delta-time encodings from one to five bytes including non-canonical forms, running status in three positions, and System Exclusive payloads with and without a terminator and with a bit-7 byte inside.

uncovered_field_names.why: Two of the declarations in the .bt carry no constraints entry. Both are struct instances rather than fields, and they are named here so the coverage audit is complete rather than merely silent.

struct_instances.reason: m_dtime is an instance of the DeltaTime struct, every byte of which is constrained under DeltaTime.t0 through DeltaTime.t3; file.header is the single instance of MidiHeader, every field of which is keyed under MidiHeader.*. Neither carries a constraint of its own. The other two DeltaTime instances, meta_event.m_length and sysex_event.m_length, ARE keyed, because they serve as length fields and carry a calculated_value contract beyond the encoding itself. MidiTrack.message is the loop variable at line 252 - one MidiMessage per iteration - and every field it can contain is keyed under MidiMessage.m_status and the nine event-struct prefixes; its repetition is governed by the MidiMessage cardinality rule in structure.

uncovered_field_names.note: The nine anonymous event structs declared inside MidiMessage - note_off_event, note_on_event, note_pressure_event, controller_event, program_event, channel_pressure_event, pitch_bend_event, meta_event and sysex_event - have no typename of their own, so their members are keyed as <instance>.<field>, which is how every key in this file resolves to a real declaration.

MidiHeader.m_magic.tier_rationale: The file's magic number. Measured, both parsers refuse anything else before reading a further byte: mido raises 'MThd not found. Probably not a MIDI file' and TiMidity++ does not recognise the file as MIDI at all, printing no Format line and rendering nothing.
MidiHeader.m_magic.description: Header chunk identifier: the four ASCII characters 'MThd' opening every Standard MIDI File.

measured_gate.observed: 'MThd' parses in both. 'MTHD', 'Mthd', 'MTrk', 'RIFF' and four zero bytes are all refused by both: mido with 'MThd not found. Probably not a MIDI file', TiMidity++ by silently declining to treat the file as MIDI.
measured_gate.conclusion: Case-sensitive and exact. The template's own header comment at line 11 records the ID bytes as 4D 54 68 64.

MidiHeader.m_magic.notes: The template does not guard this value - there is no Assert or comparison anywhere - so it is Tier A on the strength of the format and the measurement, not of any template check.

MidiHeader.m_seclen.tier_rationale: The header chunk's declared body length. A parser reads this many bytes of header before looking for the first track chunk, so a value smaller than the six bytes actually present leaves it positioned inside the header. Measured, mido raises EOFError for 0 and 5.
MidiHeader.m_seclen.description: Length in bytes of the header chunk body that follows; always 6 for a Standard MIDI File.
MidiHeader.m_seclen.algorithm: byte count of the header chunk body
MidiHeader.m_seclen.covers: m_format[2] + m_ntracks[2] + m_tickdiv[2], and any trailing header bytes a future revision adds

measured_gate.observed: 6 with a 6-byte body: both parse. 0 and 5 with a 6-byte body: mido raises EOFError. 7, 8, 10 and 100 with matching bodies: both parse, mido skipping the surplus. TiMidity++ ignores the field entirely and always reads exactly six bytes.
measured_gate.conclusion: The value must be at least 6 and must match the bytes actually emitted. SMF 1.0 fixes it at 6; larger values are forward-compatible and were measured to work, but this template declares exactly three 2-byte fields and no filler, so 6 is the only self-consistent value it can produce.

MidiHeader.m_seclen.template_parse_requirement: m_seclen is declared at line 23 and never used again - MidiHeader is a fixed six-byte body of m_format, m_ntracks and m_tickdiv, and the top-level struct goes straight from header to tracks[] with no seek. So the only value this template can emit consistently is 6. Emitting a larger header, which real parsers accept, would require adding filler fields to the struct.

MidiHeader.m_format.tier_rationale: The SMF format type. Measured as a genuine front gate in one of the two parsers: TiMidity++ refuses to recognise a file whose format is 3 or above, printing no Format line and rendering nothing, while mido accepts any 16-bit value. The legal set has exactly three members and each selects a different track-interpretation model, so all three must be emitted.
MidiHeader.m_format.description: Standard MIDI File format: 0 = one multi-channel track, 1 = simultaneous tracks sharing a timebase, 2 = independent sequential patterns.

measured_gate.observed: 0, 1 and 2 parse in both, and TiMidity++ reports the format back correctly in each case. 3, 4 and 255 are refused by TiMidity++ - no Format line, nothing rendered - while mido reports them back as type 3, 4 and 255 without complaint. 65535 comes back from mido as type -1, showing it reads the field as signed.
measured_gate.conclusion: Exactly three legal values. Format 1 and format 2 are worth emitting as much as format 0: format 1 makes a parser merge tracks against a shared timebase and format 2 makes it treat each track as an independent sequence, which are different code paths in every sequencer.

MidiHeader.m_format.notes: Declared as an anonymous enum of underlying type short at lines 24-29, so the three names are the template's own.

MidiHeader.m_ntracks.tier_rationale: The track count, and the bound of the tracks[] array at line 260. It is the repeat-controlling field of the whole format: every extra track is another MTrk chunk, another event loop and, in format 1, another voice merged against the shared timebase. Capping it would cap how much of a sequencer's multi-track machinery any file can reach.
MidiHeader.m_ntracks.description: Number of MTrk chunks that follow the header.

measured_gate.observed: A declared count matching the tracks actually present parses in both at 1, 2 and 3. A count larger than the tracks present makes mido raise EOFError while TiMidity++ tolerates it. A count of 0 makes both read no tracks at all and succeed. Declaring -1 made mido report 0 tracks, confirming it reads the field as unsigned 65535 and then finds nothing.
measured_gate.conclusion: Free, provided the declared count equals the number of MTrk chunks emitted - an agreement recorded as a dependency rather than as a bound here. Total file size is bounded by the output_budget on the tracks[] structure rule, never by capping this field.

MidiHeader.m_ntracks.notes: TEMPLATE HAZARD: declared as a signed short, so a value above 32767 becomes negative and line 260 asks for an array of negative length. The SMF specification defines the field as a 16-bit unsigned count, so the template's signedness is a transcription slip, not a format rule.

MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.tier_rationale: The timebase, and a field with two completely different meanings selected by its sign - positive is ticks per quarter note, negative is SMPTE frames and subframes. Measured free across the entire signed span in both parsers, and the sign genuinely switches code: TiMidity++ reported four different internal divisions for four different SMPTE encodings. Pinning it to a musical 96 or 480 would delete the whole SMPTE timing path.
MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.description: Delta-time unit: a positive value is ticks per quarter note; a negative value packs a negative SMPTE frame rate in the high byte and ticks per frame in the low byte.

measured_gate.observed: Positive values 1, 96, 480 and 32767 all parse in both and TiMidity++ echoes each back. The four standard SMPTE encodings - high byte -24, -25, -29 and -30 - all parse in both, and TiMidity++ converted them to internal divisions of 92, 960, 2240 and 2320 respectively, proving the SMPTE branch is live code and not a pass-through. 0, -255 (an undefined frame rate) and -32768 all parse too, though 0 made TiMidity++ expand the file to its 1048575-event ceiling.
measured_gate.conclusion: Entirely free across both signs. NO MINIMUM AND NO MAXIMUM IS RECORDED and none may be added. The event-count blow-up at tickdiv 0 is a rendering cost in one tool, not a parse gate, and is exactly the kind of observation that must not be turned into a bound - the file still parses and a generator that emits it produces a legitimate file.

MidiHeader.m_tickdiv.notes: The four SMPTE frame rates the specification defines are high bytes 0xE8 (-24), 0xE7 (-25), 0xE3 (-29, for 29.97 drop-frame) and 0xE2 (-30); the low byte is ticks per frame, conventionally 4, 8, 10, 80 or 100. Those are the values a SMPTE-aware parser branches on, and they are reachable only by leaving this field signed and free.

DeltaTime.t0.tier_rationale: The first byte of a variable-length quantity. Bit 7 is not data - it is the continuation flag that decides whether t1 exists - so a generator that treats this as a free byte produces a delta time of the wrong length and every byte after it is read as the wrong field. The value bits are free; the flag bit is structural.
DeltaTime.t0.description: First byte of the delta-time variable-length quantity: bit 7 set means another byte follows, bits 0-6 are the most significant seven bits of the value so far.

measured_gate.observed: Delta times of 0, 1 and 127 encode in one byte; 128 and 16383 in two; 16384 and 2097151 in three; 2097152 and 268435455 in four. All eight parse correctly in both parsers. A non-canonical encoding with redundant continuation bytes - 80 00 for zero, and 80 80 80 00 for zero - also parses correctly in both.
measured_gate.conclusion: Every byte value is legal here; what matters is that bit 7 agrees with whether another byte was emitted. Non-canonical encodings are accepted and are worth emitting, because they exercise the multi-byte accumulation loop for a value that would otherwise take one byte.

DeltaTime.t0.notes: The four bytes form one variable-length quantity: each carries seven bits of the value in bits 0-6, and bit 7 says whether another byte follows. The template declares exactly four, with a break after each (lines 39-40, 45-46, 51-52, 57-58), so it can express the SMF maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF in 28 bits and no more.

DeltaTime.t1.tier_rationale: The second variable-length byte, present only when t0 had bit 7 set; bit 7 here decides whether t2 exists, so the same structural rule applies.
DeltaTime.t1.description: Second byte of the delta-time variable-length quantity.
DeltaTime.t1.notes: The four bytes form one variable-length quantity: each carries seven bits of the value in bits 0-6, and bit 7 says whether another byte follows. The template declares exactly four, with a break after each (lines 39-40, 45-46, 51-52, 57-58), so it can express the SMF maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF in 28 bits and no more.

DeltaTime.t2.tier_rationale: The third variable-length byte, present only when t1 had bit 7 set; bit 7 here decides whether t3 exists.
DeltaTime.t2.description: Third byte of the delta-time variable-length quantity.
DeltaTime.t2.notes: The four bytes form one variable-length quantity: each carries seven bits of the value in bits 0-6, and bit 7 says whether another byte follows. The template declares exactly four, with a break after each (lines 39-40, 45-46, 51-52, 57-58), so it can express the SMF maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF in 28 bits and no more.

DeltaTime.t3.tier_rationale: The fourth and last byte the struct declares. Bit 7 MUST be clear here: there is no t4 field, so a set continuation bit tells a real parser to read a fifth byte that the template never emitted, and every following field is read one byte late. This is the one genuinely pinned bit in the whole delta-time encoding.
DeltaTime.t3.description: Fourth byte of the delta-time variable-length quantity; must terminate the sequence with bit 7 clear.

measured_gate.observed: A delta time encoded in five bytes (81 80 80 80 00) was read by mido as a valid quantity - it does not enforce the four-byte limit - and TiMidity++ then found only two events instead of three, having lost synchronisation. The four-byte maximum 0x0FFFFFFF encoded as FF FF FF 7F parses correctly in both.
measured_gate.conclusion: The SMF specification caps a delta time at four bytes and 0x0FFFFFFF, and this template can express no more, so the terminating byte must be the fourth at the latest. Bits 0-6 remain completely free.

DeltaTime.t3.notes: The four bytes form one variable-length quantity: each carries seven bits of the value in bits 0-6, and bit 7 says whether another byte follows. The template declares exactly four, with a break after each (lines 39-40, 45-46, 51-52, 57-58), so it can express the SMF maximum of 0x0FFFFFFF in 28 bits and no more.

MidiMessage.m_status.tier_rationale: The single most consequential byte in the format. Bit 7 decides whether this is an explicit status byte or a running-status continuation, and the high nibble then selects which of the nine event structures the template reads - so a wrong value does not mis-record a value, it makes the parser read the wrong number of bytes and lose the stream. Measured, the values outside the legal set are refused by mido with 'undefined status byte' or a byte-count error.
MidiMessage.m_status.description: MIDI status byte: 0x80-0xEF are channel voice messages with the channel in the low nibble, 0xF0 and 0xF7 introduce System Exclusive data, 0xFF introduces a meta event, and a value below 0x80 is not a status byte at all but the first data byte of a running-status message.

measured_gate.observed: All 112 channel voice statuses 0x80-0xEF parse in both parsers; note off, note on, polyphonic pressure, controller, program change, channel pressure and pitch bend were each exercised on channels 0, 5 and 15. 0xF0 and 0xF7 with a length prefix parse in both. 0xFF introduces a meta event and parses in both. The excluded values do not: 0xF4 and 0xF5 give mido 'undefined status byte'; 0xF2 gives 'data byte must be in range 0..127'; 0xF6, 0xF8, 0xFA and 0xFE give 'wrong number of bytes for tune_request / clock / start / active_sensing'; 0xF1 and 0xF3 are read as System Common messages of a different length, which desynchronised mido into reporting three events where two were emitted. TiMidity++ consumed all of them without producing a playable event.
measured_gate.conclusion: The legal set for a Standard MIDI File is 0x80-0xEF, 0xF0, 0xF7 and 0xFF, plus 0x00-0x7F for running status. The excluded_values are System Common and System Real-Time messages which exist on the wire but are not permitted in a file, and which the template nevertheless routes to sysex_event - see the note.

MidiMessage.m_status.notes: SIGNEDNESS: the field is declared 'char', which is signed in 010 Editor, so these values appear negative internally; line 127 tests lastStatus == -1 for the meta-event status 0xFF, and lines 73 to 236 mask with 0xf0 after integer promotion. valid_values are recorded as unsigned byte values because that is what a generator writes.\nRUNNING STATUS: line 67 tests bit 7. When it is clear the template seeks back one byte (line 70) and reuses lastStatus, which is how a running-status message is parsed. Values 0x00-0x7F are therefore legal here but only when a previous message set lastStatus - see the dependencies and the structure rules.\nTEMPLATE GAP: line 236 routes every status whose high nibble is 0xF to sysex_event, which reads a DeltaTime length and that many bytes. That is correct for 0xF0 and 0xF7 and wrong for the twelve excluded values, which carry either no payload or a fixed one-to-two byte payload and no length prefix at all. That is why they are excluded rather than merely deprecated.

note_off_event.m_note.tier_rationale: A MIDI data byte. Bit 7 must be clear or the byte is read as a status byte and the event stream desynchronises; measured, mido refuses the file with 'data byte must be in range 0..127'.
note_off_event.m_note.description: Key number of the note being released, 0-127 with 60 as middle C.

measured_gate.observed: A note-on whose note byte is 0xFF, and one whose velocity byte is 0x80, are both refused by mido with 'data byte must be in range 0..127'. TiMidity++ tolerates both. Every combination inside 0-127 that was tried - note 0/64/127 against velocity 0/1/127 - parses in both.
measured_gate.conclusion: One of the two parsers refuses the file outright, so the top bit is Tier A. The remaining seven bits are free and every value 0-127 was measured to work.

note_off_event.m_note.notes: MIDI's one universal invariant: a data byte has bit 7 CLEAR. A byte with bit 7 set is by definition a status byte, so writing 128-255 here does not merely record an out-of-range value - it injects a status byte into the middle of an event and every byte after it is read as the wrong field. The seven value bits are completely free; only the top bit is pinned. This is the 'pin the envelope, free the contents' shape at byte scale.

sysex_event.m_message.tier_rationale: The template declares this as a bare char array sized by a length field and says nothing about its contents - the situation checklist item 3 exists for. Its bytes are a System Exclusive message, whose defining rule is that every data byte has bit 7 clear and the message ends with 0xF7. Measured, a single byte with bit 7 set inside the payload makes mido refuse the file with 'data byte must be in range 0..127'.
sysex_event.m_message.description: System Exclusive payload: manufacturer identifier, device and command bytes, and a terminating 0xF7.
sysex_event.m_message.codec: MIDI System Exclusive message (MMA MIDI 1.0 Detailed Specification, section on System Exclusive; carried in an SMF per the Standard MIDI Files 1.0 specification)
sysex_event.m_message.must_produce:
Every byte of the payload must have bit 7 CLEAR - values 0x00 to 0x7F - except the final byte, which is the End Of Exclusive terminator 0xF7. The 0xF0 that introduced the event is NOT part of this array; the template consumed it as m_status, and the length counts only what follows the length field itself.
The payload's own layout is:
  MANUFACTURER ID   one byte 0x01-0x7C, or the three-byte form 0x00 followed by two more bytes; the special values are 0x7D (non-commercial), 0x7E (Universal Non-Real Time) and 0x7F (Universal Real Time).
  DEVICE ID         one byte, 0x7F meaning 'all devices'.
  SUB-ID / DATA     any number of 7-bit bytes, meaning defined by the manufacturer.
  TERMINATOR        0xF7.
A payload split across several events uses 0xF7 as the status byte of each continuation, and only the final one carries the terminator - the template routes 0xF7 to this same struct, so both halves are expressible.
sysex_event.m_message.decoder_gate: Measured against mido 1.x and TiMidity++. A payload containing a byte with bit 7 set - 7E FF 09 01 F7 - is refused outright by mido with 'ValueError: data byte must be in range 0..127', so nothing in the file after that point is parsed. TiMidity++ tolerates it but produces no System Exclusive event. A payload with all-7-bit bytes and an 0xF7 terminator parses in both. Omitting the terminator was tolerated by both, as was an empty payload and a 201-byte one, so the terminator is a specification requirement rather than a measured gate, while the 7-bit rule is a measured gate.
sysex_event.m_message.generation_strategy:
The simplest correct payload is the Universal Non-Real Time Identity Request, five bytes, which every MIDI device understands:
  7E   Universal Non-Real Time manufacturer id
  7F   device id, all devices
  06   sub-id 1, General Information
  01   sub-id 2, Identity Request
  F7   End Of Exclusive
emitted as status 0xF0, then the variable-length length 05, then those five bytes. Verified to parse in both parsers.
To vary it while staying correct, keep the shape and change the contents: pick any manufacturer id from 0x01-0x7C, or 0x00 plus two more bytes for the extended form, then any number of bytes drawn from 0x00-0x7F, then 0xF7. Set m_length to the total emitted. The payload length is chosen freely and m_length is computed from it - never the reverse.
sysex_event.m_message.notes: This is the format's only opaque array with required internal structure. Every other byte run in the template - the nine text meta events and m_data - is genuinely free-form, which is recorded on each of those entries rather than left implicit.

MidiTrack.m_magic.notes: The SMF specification says an unrecognised chunk type should be skipped using its length, which is what makes the four-byte identifier plus a length a general chunk framing rather than a fixed layout.

MidiTrack.m_seclen.tier_rationale: The track chunk's byte length, and the loop budget at lines 250-254: the template subtracts each message's size from it and stops when it reaches zero. Measured, a value one byte either side of the truth makes mido raise EOFError, because the next chunk header is looked for at the wrong offset.
MidiTrack.m_seclen.description: Length in bytes of the track's event data, not counting the eight bytes of chunk identifier and length.
MidiTrack.m_seclen.algorithm: byte count of all the MidiMessage records in this track
MidiTrack.m_seclen.covers: every byte from the first delta time of the first message to the last byte of the end-of-track meta event

measured_gate.observed: The exact length parses in both. One byte short, one byte long, and a thousand bytes long all make mido raise EOFError. A length of 0 is legal and produced an empty track in both. TiMidity++ tolerated every mismatch by resynchronising on the next MTrk.
measured_gate.conclusion: Must equal the sum of the message sizes exactly. Zero is legal and worth emitting - an empty track exercises the zero-iteration path of every track loop.

MidiTrack.m_seclen.template_parse_requirement: TEMPLATE HAZARD at lines 250-254: 'local uint remaining = m_seclen;' then 'while (remaining) { MidiMessage message; remaining -= sizeof(message); }'. Because remaining is unsigned and the loop tests for exactly zero, a m_seclen that is not the exact sum of the message sizes makes the subtraction underflow to a value near 2^32 and the loop runs away. The generator must compute this field from the messages it emitted, never choose it independently.

file.tracks.description: The MTrk chunks of the file, one per track declared in the header.
file.tracks.notes: Declared with <optimize=false> because each track has a different length. The number of chunks emitted must equal header.m_ntracks - measured, mido raises EOFError when it is short - which is recorded as a dependency rather than as a bound on either field.

then.detail: exactly m_ntracks MTrk chunks must follow the header, no more and no fewer

dependencies.description: The declared track count must equal the number of track chunks actually emitted.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: declaring 2 or 3 tracks with only one present makes mido raise EOFError; TiMidity++ tolerates the mismatch and renders what it finds. Declaring 0 makes both read no tracks and succeed. Extra MTrk chunks beyond the declared count were ignored by both.
dependencies.note: This is the derive-the-structure-from-the-count rule: emit the tracks, then write the count, or pick the count and emit exactly that many - never let them drift.

then.detail: the SMF specification requires exactly 1 track in a format 0 file

dependencies.description: A format 0 file holds a single multi-channel track by definition.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a format 0 file declaring 2 tracks with 2 tracks present parsed in BOTH parsers without complaint. So the rule comes from the specification and is not enforced, which is why m_ntracks stays Tier C and this dependency is advisory.
dependencies.note: Worth violating occasionally: a format 0 file with several tracks is legal as far as every parser measured is concerned and exercises the multi-track merge path under a format that claims not to need it.

then.detail: delta times are counted in SMPTE subframes rather than in ticks per quarter note, and META_TEMPO has no effect on timing

dependencies.description: A negative timebase switches the whole file from musical to absolute SMPTE time.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: the four standard SMPTE encodings (-24, -25, -29, -30 in the high byte) all parsed in both parsers, and TiMidity++ converted them to four different internal divisions - 92, 960, 2240 and 2320 - proving the SMPTE branch is live code rather than a pass-through.
dependencies.note: Both timing models must be emitted; they are different arithmetic in every sequencer.

then.detail: a byte below 0x80 is a running-status continuation and is legal ONLY when an earlier message in the same track already set an explicit status

dependencies.description: Running status reuses the previous status byte, so it cannot appear before one has been established.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a track whose first event omits the status byte is refused by mido with 'running status without last_status'. The same omission after an explicit note-on parses correctly in both parsers, and two consecutive running-status events also parse.
dependencies.note: TEMPLATE HAZARD: lastStatus is initialised to 0 at line 61, so a leading running-status byte makes the template take none of the nine branches at lines 73-243, read no event payload at all, and subtract only the delta time from the track's remaining budget.

then.detail: the NEXT message must carry an explicit status byte; running status is cancelled by any System Exclusive or meta event

dependencies.description: System and meta messages clear running status, so the following event cannot rely on it.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a note-on followed by a System Exclusive event and then a running-status event is refused by mido with EOFError. The same sequence with a meta event in place of the sysex was tolerated by mido but is still a template desynchroniser - see the note.
dependencies.note: TEMPLATE DESYNC: line 68 sets lastStatus to 0xFF for a meta event, so a following running-status byte makes the template re-enter the meta branch at line 127 and read that data byte as a meta TYPE and the next as a variable-length LENGTH. A running-status pair such as 62 100 becomes 'meta type 0x3E, length 100' and swallows the next 100 bytes.

then.detail: exactly two data bytes follow, each with bit 7 clear

dependencies.description: Note off, note on, polyphonic pressure, controller and pitch bend messages all carry two data bytes.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: all four families were exercised on channels 0, 5 and 15 and parsed in both parsers; a data byte with bit 7 set is refused by mido with 'data byte must be in range 0..127'.

then.detail: exactly ONE data byte follows, with bit 7 clear

dependencies.description: Program change and channel pressure messages carry a single data byte, unlike every other channel voice message.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: program change and channel pressure on channels 0, 5 and 15 all parsed in both parsers with one data byte each.
dependencies.note: This is the asymmetry a generator is most likely to get wrong, because seven of the nine channel voice families take two data bytes and these two take one.

then.detail: a meta type byte and a variable-length length follow, and the length must match the payload

dependencies.description: The 0xFF status introduces a meta event rather than a channel message.
dependencies.note: Line 127 tests lastStatus == -1 rather than 0xFF because m_status is a signed char; the test precedes the 0xF0 family test at line 236, which is what keeps 0xFF out of the sysex branch.

dependencies.description: An end-of-track event carries no payload, so its length must be zero.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: an end-of-track declaring length 1 with one payload byte was tolerated by both parsers, so this is a specification rule rather than an enforced gate - but the template's branch at lines 201-203 is empty, so any non-zero length leaves those bytes unconsumed and the track length arithmetic wrong.

dependencies.description: A tempo event carries exactly three bytes of microseconds per quarter note.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: declaring 2 instead of 3 makes mido fail with IndexError; declaring 4 was tolerated by mido but leaves the template's compensating seek at line 208 pointing at the wrong byte.

dependencies.description: An SMPTE offset event carries exactly five bytes: hours, minutes, seconds, frames and fractional frames.
A time signature event carries exactly four bytes: numerator, denominator exponent, clocks per click and thirty-seconds per quarter.
A key signature event carries exactly two bytes: the accidental count and the mode.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: with the correct two-byte payload, accidental counts -7 to 7 and modes 0 and 1 all parse; outside those, mido raises KeySignatureError.

dependencies.description: A sequence number event carries exactly two bytes.
dependencies.note: The specification also permits a zero-length sequence number event meaning 'use the track's position'; the template's branch at line 155 always reads a short, so this template can only express the two-byte form.

dependencies.description: The MIDI channel prefix and MIDI port events each carry exactly one byte.

then.detail: the payload is m_length bytes of free text, of any length including zero

dependencies.description: The nine text meta events carry a variable-length string whose size is whatever the length field says.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: all nine text types parsed in both parsers; a length disagreeing with the bytes present makes mido fail with EOFError or a running-status error.

then.detail: a variable-length length follows, then that many bytes, all with bit 7 clear except a final 0xF7 terminator

dependencies.description: System Exclusive events in a file carry an explicit length rather than relying on the terminator alone.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a payload containing a byte with bit 7 set is refused by mido with 'data byte must be in range 0..127'. An empty payload, a 201-byte payload and a payload without the terminator were all tolerated by both parsers.
dependencies.note: 0xF7 as a status byte introduces either a continuation of a split System Exclusive message or an escaped sequence of arbitrary bytes; the template routes both to the same struct.

then.detail: t1 exists only when t0 has bit 7 set, and the same chain relates t1 to t2 and t2 to t3

dependencies.description: The delta-time byte count is self-describing through the continuation bit.
dependencies.note: Lines 39-40, 45-46 and 51-52 break out of the struct as soon as a byte with bit 7 clear is read, so the field count is decided by the data, not declared anywhere.

structure.subject: MidiHeader
structure.detail: The MThd chunk must be the first thing in the file, and its four identifier bytes must be the first four bytes.
structure.description: A Standard MIDI File opens with the header chunk.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: both parsers refuse a file that does not begin with 'MThd'; mido says so explicitly, TiMidity++ declines to treat the file as MIDI.
structure.generation_note: Emit MThd, the length 6, then format, ntracks and tickdiv as a fixed head element. Write m_ntracks after the tracks are laid out, or decide it first and emit exactly that many.

structure.subject: MidiTrack
structure.detail: At least one MTrk chunk should follow the header, and each begins with its own four-byte identifier and length.
structure.description: The music lives in track chunks; a header alone carries no events.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a file declaring 0 tracks parses in both parsers and produces nothing. A track whose identifier is not 'MTrk' is refused by mido and skipped entirely by TiMidity++.
structure.generation_note: Emit each track as identifier, length, then the event stream; compute the length from the bytes emitted.

structure.subject: MidiHeader before file.tracks
structure.detail: The header chunk precedes every track chunk; there is no other ordering freedom at file level.
structure.description: SMF is a flat chunk sequence with a mandatory first chunk.
structure.generation_note: Lay the file out in order. Unlike RIFF or PNG there is no nesting, so the offsets are simply cumulative.

structure.subject: file.tracks
structure.detail: The tracks array repeats exactly header.m_ntracks times.
structure.description: Track chunks are the file-level repeating structure.
structure.output_budget: Budget the whole file to about 256 KB, as a running total the generator increments by each track's full size - 8 bytes of chunk framing plus the event bytes - and checks before starting another track. When the budget is exhausted, stop adding tracks and write m_ntracks to match what was emitted. Neither m_ntracks nor m_tickdiv nor any delta time is capped to achieve this.
structure.generation_note: Emit the header, then a repeated array of MTrk chunks bounded by output_budget, then nothing - the file ends with the last track.

structure.subject: MidiMessage within a MidiTrack
structure.detail: A track body is a run of messages consumed until the declared length is exhausted; the loop at lines 251-254 subtracts each message's size from the remaining budget.
structure.description: Events are the inner repeating structure and the bulk of every MIDI file.
structure.output_budget: Budget each track's event stream to about 64 KB, as a running total the generator increments by each message's encoded size. When the budget is exhausted, emit the end-of-track meta event and stop. Delta times, note values and payload lengths are never trimmed to fit - the generator simply stops adding messages.
structure.generation_note: Emit messages while the budget allows, then the end-of-track event, then set MidiTrack.m_seclen from the total bytes emitted. The first message must carry an explicit status byte.

structure.subject: MidiMessage.m_status within a track
structure.detail: The first message of every track must carry an explicit status byte, with bit 7 set.
structure.description: Running status has nothing to continue from at the start of a track.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a track whose first event omits the status byte is refused by mido with 'running status without last_status'. The template reads no event payload at all in that case, because lastStatus is still 0.
structure.generation_note: Force bit 7 on the first message's status byte; from the second message onwards running status is a free choice.

structure.subject: meta_event with m_type META_END_OF_TRACK
structure.detail: Every track should end with an FF 2F 00 end-of-track meta event, and nothing may follow it inside the chunk.
structure.description: The end-of-track event is how the specification marks the end of a track's event stream.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: omitting it entirely was tolerated by both parsers, and events placed after it were still parsed by mido while TiMidity++ stopped at it. So it is a specification requirement that neither parser enforces - but emitting it is what makes the two agree.
structure.generation_note: Emit it as a fixed tail of every track, with delta time of your choosing and length zero.

structure.subject: MidiTrack event stream
structure.detail: The messages of a track run contiguously from the end of the chunk length to the end of the chunk, with no padding or separators.
structure.description: MIDI has no inter-event framing: the length of each message is implied by its status byte.
structure.generation_note: Nothing may be inserted between messages. This is why a single wrong data byte desynchronises everything after it.

structure.subject: MidiTrack.m_seclen exactness
structure.detail: The declared track length must equal the exact byte count of the messages emitted.
structure.description: The track length is the only way a parser knows where one track ends and the next begins.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: one byte short, one byte long, and a thousand bytes long all make mido raise EOFError. TiMidity++ resynchronises on the next MTrk identifier.
structure.generation_note: Compute it after emitting the messages. The template's loop subtracts from an unsigned counter and tests for exactly zero, so an inexact value underflows and runs away.

structure.subject: running status immediately after a meta or System Exclusive event
structure.detail: A message following an FF, F0 or F7 event must carry its own status byte.
structure.description: System and meta messages cancel running status.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: note-on, then System Exclusive, then a running-status event is refused by mido with EOFError. After a meta event mido tolerated it, but the template misreads it as a nested meta event and swallows up to 127 bytes.
structure.generation_note: Track the last channel status in the generator and clear it whenever a 0xFF, 0xF0 or 0xF7 event is emitted.

structure.subject: a fifth delta-time byte
structure.detail: A delta time must terminate within four bytes; the terminating byte has bit 7 clear.
structure.description: SMF caps a delta time at 0x0FFFFFFF, which is 28 bits and four seven-bit bytes.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a five-byte encoding was read as valid by mido but cost TiMidity++ synchronisation, which then found two events where three were emitted. The template declares only four bytes.
structure.generation_note: Encode the value with the standard variable-length algorithm, which never exceeds four bytes for a value below 2^28.

structure.subject: the nine MidiMessage event branches
structure.detail: Exactly one of note_off_event, note_on_event, note_pressure_event, controller_event, program_event, channel_pressure_event, pitch_bend_event, meta_event and sysex_event is present per message, selected by the status byte.
structure.description: The message body is one branch of a nine-way if/else chain on the status byte's high nibble.
structure.generation_note: Choose the status byte first, then emit the matching body with the matching number of data bytes.

structure.subject: trailing data after the last track
structure.detail: The format defines nothing after the final track chunk.
structure.description: There is no trailer or index at the end of a MIDI file.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: twenty bytes of junk appended after the last track were ignored by both parsers, as was an extra MTrk chunk beyond the declared count.
structure.generation_note: Both are tolerated, so trailing bytes are a legitimate source of variety - but they are not part of the format and no parser will read them.

diversity_axes.why: The track count, and the file-level repeat bound. Every extra track is another chunk header, another event loop and, under format 1, another voice merged against the shared timebase. Capping it is the single easiest way to make every generated file look the same.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Decides how many times a parser runs its chunk loop and, in format 1, how much of the multi-track merge and tempo-map machinery runs. A count of 0 exercises the zero-track path, which most files never reach.

diversity_axes.why: The timebase, and the one field whose SIGN changes the meaning of every delta time in the file from musical ticks to SMPTE subframes. Measured, the four SMPTE encodings produce four different internal divisions in TiMidity++, so this is live code and not a pass-through. Pinning it to 96 or 480 deletes the entire absolute-time path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Positive values drive the tempo-scaled tick arithmetic and make META_TEMPO meaningful; negative values drive the SMPTE frame and subframe arithmetic, where tempo is ignored. The two are different computations in every sequencer.

diversity_axes.why: The file's track-interpretation model. Format 0 merges everything into one track, format 1 treats tracks as simultaneous against a shared timebase, and format 2 treats each as an independent pattern. Emitting only format 0 - the obvious safe choice - deletes two whole interpretation models.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects between single-track playback, multi-track merge against track 1's tempo map, and independent sequential patterns.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because TiMidity++ refuses formats above 2 outright, but all three legal values are free choices and all three must be emitted - 'unconstrained' here means do not narrow to the convenient member.

diversity_axes.why: The event type, the channel, and whether running status is used - three free choices packed into one byte. It decides how many bytes the message occupies, so it is the field that shapes the entire event stream. Narrowing it to note-on and note-off would delete seven of the nine event structures.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The high nibble selects one of nine parser branches with one, two or variable-length payloads. The low nibble selects the channel, and a synthesiser keeps separate state per channel. Omitting the status byte entirely selects the running-status path, which is a different branch again.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because values outside the legal set are refused by mido, but the legal set has 243 members and every one of them is a free choice.

diversity_axes.why: The delta time, and with it the encoded length of every event. A generator that always emits zero produces one-byte delta times forever and never exercises the multi-byte accumulation loop; a generator that varies the value freely produces one-, two-, three- and four-byte encodings and reaches all of it. Measured, non-canonical encodings are accepted too.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The value drives the accumulation loop once per continuation byte. It also drives the sequencer's event scheduling: a zero delta makes events simultaneous, a large one makes the renderer emit silence, and the two take different paths through the event queue.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A for the continuation-bit structure; the seven value bits of each byte are entirely free and must stay so.

diversity_axes.why: The meta-event type, selecting among eighteen named payload layouts plus a catch-all. Several - tempo, time signature, key signature, SMPTE offset - change how the rest of the file is interpreted rather than merely recording data.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Tempo rewrites the tick-to-microsecond conversion for everything after it; SMPTE offset sets the absolute start; key and time signature drive notation code; the text types drive string handling; undefined types drive the skip-by-length path.

diversity_axes.why: The tempo. It multiplies through every delta time in the file, so it changes the rendered timeline globally. Measured free across the whole 24-bit span including 0. Pinning it to the 500000 default is the textbook needless narrowing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Rewrites the tick-to-real-time conversion; extreme values drive the renderer's clamping and overflow handling, and a tempo event mid-track forces a tempo-map rebuild.

diversity_axes.why: The track length. Its value is fixed by the messages emitted, but HOW MANY messages a track carries is entirely free, and that is what this length records. A length of 0 is legal and exercises the empty-track path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds the event loop; zero takes the no-iteration path and a large value keeps the parser in the event loop for the whole chunk.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a length that must be exact, but the message count it records is a free choice that must not be fixed.

diversity_axes.why: Attack velocity, and the field with a special case worth reaching: a note-on with velocity 0 is treated as a note-off by essentially every synthesiser, which is a distinct branch no non-zero velocity reaches. Measured free across 0-127.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Velocity scales the rendered amplitude and selects velocity layers in a sampler; zero diverts to the note-off path entirely.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A only for the top bit, which must be clear; all 128 values below that are free and all of them matter.

diversity_axes.why: The controller number. Values 120-127 are Channel Mode messages - All Sound Off, All Notes Off, Omni and Mono/Poly switching - which drive completely different code from an ordinary continuous controller, and they are exactly the high awkward values a narrowing pass would discard.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0-119 set continuous controller state; 120-127 are Channel Mode messages that reset voices, silence the channel or change the voice allocation model.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A only for the top bit; the 128 values below it are free and the top eight are the most valuable.

diversity_axes.why: The System Exclusive payload length. How long a SysEx message is, and whether it is split across several events, is a free choice; the length simply records it. Measured, 0 and 201 both parse.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives the payload read loop; zero takes the empty-message path and a long payload exercises the buffer growth a short one never does.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a length that must match the payload, but the payload size it records is free.

diversity_axes.why: The header chunk length. SMF fixes it at 6 and this template can emit nothing else, but real parsers accept larger headers and skip the surplus - measured at 7, 8, 10 and 100 - which is a forward compatibility path worth knowing about.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A value above 6 makes a parser skip the surplus bytes, exercising the forward-compatibility branch that a conforming 6-byte header never reaches.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A and effectively pinned to 6 by this template's fixed struct; listed here because the format itself leaves room that a rewritten template could use.
